data.narrative:
TerraFirma is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $115M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable, spanning seed through Series B stages. The most relevant peers—Humanoid ($1.4B Series A), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), and Dexterity ($1.6B Series B)—provide direct stage and sector context.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $115M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding $230M. Peer-median analysis across the five most comparable firms (including Humanoid at Series A, Walden Robotics at seed, and three Series B companies) produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The stage-progression method reflects a conservative anchor tied directly to capital deployed; the peer-median reflects market pricing for similar-stage robotics companies but includes stage and maturity variation.

The two methods yield a wide implied range: $230M (stage-progression) to $1.6B (peer-median). A triangulated midpoint of $940M sits materially above stage-progression but below the peer-median, reflecting TerraFirma's position as an earlier-stage entrant in a cohort where Series B valuations have reached $1.8B–$2.0B. Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to peers and execution risk typical of Series A. The analysis supports a valuation range of $196M to $1.9B, with greatest confidence in the $700M–$1.2B band.
